title: AI Substitution Exposure Rubric
orientation: Every dimension is oriented so that 5 means MAXIMUM exposure. There are no inverted dimensions. If a dimension name ever reads in the opposite direction to its scale, the name is wrong, not the scale.
weights_disclaimer: The composite weights are judgment, not a measured finding. No source in the corpus establishes the relative contribution of any dimension to substitution risk. They default to equal and are adjustable, and the report says so.

dimensions.name: Output determinism
dimensions.question: How templatable is the thing you actually hand over?
dimensions.high_means: The deliverable is a predictable artifact a model can produce a competent version of on the first try.
dimensions.evidence_note: Routine, low-complexity, repetitive output is repeatedly identified as the most eroded category. Directional across sources, with no per-service-line figure anywhere in the corpus.

anchors.1: Every engagement produces something structurally different. No two deliverables share a template.
anchors.2: Recognisable shape, but the substance is rebuilt each time and depends on discovery.
anchors.3: Templated skeleton, custom substance. A model gets the frame right and the content wrong.
anchors.4: Largely templatable. A model produces a usable draft that needs an expert edit.
anchors.5: Fully templatable. A model produces a shippable version on the first try. Logos, landing pages, blog posts, ad variations.

dimensions.name: Client self-service
dimensions.question: Can the buyer already do this themselves with a tool they have?
dimensions.high_means: A mainstream tool puts an acceptable version of this deliverable inside the client's own team.
dimensions.evidence_note: Firefly, Canva Magic Studio and equivalents are established as mainstream in 2026 design stacks, and client in-housing is named as a force alongside AI commoditization. That these specific tools displace this specific service line is inference, not a documented finding.

anchors.1: Requires capability the client has no route to acquiring. Specialist skill, licence, or scale.
anchors.2: Client could technically attempt it and would produce something they would not ship.
anchors.3: A capable client generalist gets to roughly half your quality with a mainstream tool.
anchors.4: Client's existing team can produce an acceptable version. They keep you for speed and taste, not capability.
anchors.5: One person on the client's team does this in an afternoon with a tool they already pay for.

dimensions.name: Judgment thinness
dimensions.question: How little taste, strategy or stakeholder orchestration is in the value?
dimensions.high_means: The work is execution. Almost none of what the client pays for is judgment.
dimensions.evidence_note: Strategy, taste and feedback-rich work is consistently described as retaining value while execution is hollowed out. Directional and repeated across independent sources; no source quantifies the boundary.

anchors.1: Almost entirely judgment. Framing the problem, aligning stakeholders, deciding what not to do.
anchors.2: Judgment-led. Execution follows from a decision that is the actual deliverable.
anchors.3: Even split. A defensible call up front, then substantial production behind it.
anchors.4: Mostly production. The judgment is a small number of early decisions inside a known playbook.
anchors.5: Pure execution against a brief someone else wrote. The judgment happened before you were hired.

dimensions.name: Artifact billing
dimensions.question: Are you paid for a deliverable, or for a business result you are on the hook for?
dimensions.high_means: The client buys an artifact. Nobody measures whether it worked, and you carry no consequence if it did not.
dimensions.evidence_note: The claim that accountable delivery is the defensible position rests on a single practitioner argument, supported directionally by the outcome-pricing commentary. It is reasoning, not measurement. Treat this dimension as the weakest-evidenced of the five.

anchors.1: Paid on a realized business outcome with a defined metric, baseline and window. You lose money if it fails.
anchors.2: Formal accountability for a result, with commercial consequence short of full risk transfer.
anchors.3: Result is discussed and reported on, but the invoice does not move if it misses.
anchors.4: Paid on delivery. Success is measured, informally, and nothing follows from it.
anchors.5: Paid on delivery of an artifact. No outcome is defined, tracked or owned by anyone.

dimensions.name: Price anchor erosion
dimensions.question: Is the going rate for this line visibly falling?
dimensions.high_means: Clients are asking for the AI discount on this line and competitors are quoting materially less.
dimensions.evidence_note: AI compresses delivery 3-4x, which under time-and-materials hands the entire productivity gain to the client. 60% of US marketing leaders are spending less on agencies, and Big Six share fell from 44.6% to 29.6%. These are market-level figures. No source breaks price erosion down by service line.

anchors.1: Rate has held or risen. No client has raised AI in a pricing conversation on this line.
anchors.2: Rate holding, with occasional pressure you have been able to defend.
anchors.3: Winning at the old rate is getting harder. You have started discounting to close.
anchors.4: Rate is visibly down. Clients reference AI when negotiating this line specifically.
anchors.5: Rate is collapsing. You are quoting materially less than two years ago and still losing on price.
